title: Mindset matters: Fostering teachers’ responsible AI use through professional development
venue: Journal of New Approaches in Educational Research
extended_summary:
This study asks whether professional development for future teachers about generative AI is more effective when it includes not only tool training, but also a mindset component focused on ethics, human-centered pedagogy, and critical reflection. The authors frame the problem as a gap in teacher AI preparation: most PD is tool-centric and may increase confidence without sufficiently developing responsible, reflective AI use.

The intervention was a one-day PD workshop with two conditions. One group received tools-only training on using generative AI for teaching tasks. The other group received the same tools training plus a mindset module covering AI ethics, human-centered education, growth mindset, and pedagogical reflection. The study used a mixed-method randomized design with 57 preservice teachers in a teacher education program in Vietnam. Data came from pre/post surveys measuring AI anxiety and AI competence self-efficacy, plus written reflections analyzed qualitatively.

Results showed that both groups had reduced AI anxiety after training, but the tools-only group showed broader gains in self-efficacy across multiple AI competence dimensions. The mindset-inclusive group showed a more limited quantitative gain, mainly in human-centered AI competence, but their written reflections showed deeper ethical awareness, more caution about AI limitations, and stronger attention to pedagogical responsibility. The authors conclude that mindset-oriented PD may not produce immediate boosts in confidence, but it better supports reflective, ethically grounded AI use, and should be integrated alongside technical training in teacher preparation.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic generative AI/chatbot system used for creating teaching materials and supporting teacher work; no specific commercial product is named in the paper.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in a one-day professional development workshop for preservice teachers; one condition received tools-only training on efficient use of GenAI in teaching and learning, and the comparison condition also received mindset-oriented content on ethics and human-centered pedagogy.

findings.finding_summary: In a mixed-method pre-post comparison with 57 preservice teachers, both groups showed reduced AI anxiety over time, but only the tools-only group had a statistically significant pre-post decrease. The overall Time effect was significant (b=-0.49, p=.003, η2p=.05), while the Time×Group interaction was not significant (p=.128).

Overall competence self-efficacy did not differ significantly by time or group, but the tools-only group showed a significant pre-post increase in self-efficacy, whereas the mindset-inclusive group did not. At the subscale level, the mindset-inclusive group showed a significant gain only in Human-Centered Education, while the tools-only group improved in AI Knowledge, AI Pedagogy, AI Assessment, Human-Centered Education, and Professional Engagement.
findings.measure: TAICS competence self-efficacy scale and six subscales (AI Knowledge, AI Pedagogy, AI Assessment, AI Ethics, Human-Centered Education, Professional Engagement)
findings.effect_size: motivation predictor η2p=.11; subscale effects not pooled

quality_tier_rationale: This is a small mixed-method experimental study with pre-post measures and random assignment, but outcomes are self-reported and immediate post-test only. The paper provides useful comparative evidence on teacher PD, yet it is not a fully powered RCT with long-term or behavioral validation.
impact_tier_rationale: The quantitative effects are modest and uneven: anxiety reduction is small (η2p=.05) and broader self-efficacy gains are limited to specific subdomains rather than a strong overall effect. The qualitative findings suggest meaningful reflective benefits from mindset-inclusive training, but the evidence does not show clear large impact on actual teacher uptake or classroom implementation.
